findings.title: STACK_RESERVE macro is dead in stack.c while mm.c hardcodes the same 8 MiB value
findings.detail: stack.c line 20 defines `#define STACK_RESERVE (8ull * 1024 * 1024)` but the macro is never expanded in code -- build_initial_stack() starts at `w.p = (char*)(uintptr_t) mem_size` (line 80) and the only other mention is inside the line-72 comment. Meanwhile mm.c line 40 re-derives the identical value as a magic literal: `g_mmap_top = mem_size - (8ull * 1024 * 1024); /* stack.c's STACK_RESERVE */` -- the comment itself admits it is duplicating stack.c's constant. Grep across runtime/, src/, scripts/ shows exactly these two sites. The mmap-arena ceiling and the stack reservation MUST stay equal (mm.h's own doc: 'mem_size minus stack.h's 8 MiB stack reservation'), so the constant should live once in stack.h (e.g. `#define VLINUX_STACK_RESERVE ...`) and be used by mm_init(); today a change to one silently desynchronizes the other.
findings.safety: Pure constant relocation: the numeric value (8 MiB) is unchanged at both sites, so the compiled vlinux.elf is byte-identical modulo the macro name. No control flow or data changes.
findings.verify_with: make -C runtime/linux, then tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_mmap.sh (mmap arena ceiling) and tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_glibc_hello.sh (initial stack build); tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_runtime_linux.sh covers the driver path.

findings.title: mm.h says 'MAP_SHARED is not supported (-ENOSYS)' but mm.c accepts read-only MAP_SHARED
findings.detail: The sys_mmap doc comment in mm.h (the sentence 'MAP_SHARED is not supported (-ENOSYS): this relay has no way to write a shared mapping's changes back to the host file', lines 29-31 of the block above the line-33 prototype) contradicts the implementation: mm.c lines 84-85 explicitly accept MAP_SHARED when PROT_WRITE is clear (`if (flags & MAP_SHARED) { if (prot & PROT_WRITE) return -ENOSYS; }`) and mm.c's own comment (lines 74-83) documents why -- llama.cpp's llama-mmap.cpp maps GGUF files MAP_SHARED + PROT_READ only. Only a WRITABLE MAP_SHARED request is refused. The header comment predates the llama.cpp fix and now misleads anyone reading the public contract.
findings.safety: Comment-only change in a header; no code is touched, so no behavior can change.
findings.verify_with: Comment change: compile via make -C runtime/linux; tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_mmap.sh and tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_llama_smoke.sh exercise the MAP_SHARED read-only path.

findings.title: sys_statx duplicates sys_fstatat's entire VH_SYS_FSTATAT host round-trip
findings.detail: sys_fstatat (syscall.c lines 335-344) and sys_statx (lines 359-365) contain the identical 4-step sequence: `htif_win_store_str(0, path)`, the `stoff == (size_t)-1 || stoff + 24 > WIN_DATA_SIZE` bound check, `htif_syscall(VH_SYS_FSTATAT, dirfd, WIN_DATA_VA, WIN_DATA_VA + stoff, flags)`, then `host_stat_mode_size(stoff, &mode, &size)` on success -- only the final struct-fill differs (vlinux_stat vs vlinux_statx). A static helper like `stat_host_roundtrip(dirfd, path, flags, &mode, &size)` returning the syscall result would leave each caller with just its fill code, and keep the fragile 8-aligned +24 scratch-block convention (documented at line 337) in exactly one place.
findings.safety: Extract-function refactor with no reordering: the same calls execute in the same order with the same arguments; both callers already treat r==0 as the only fill case. Static, single-TU change.
findings.verify_with: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_file.sh -- its fixture rt_linux_file.c explicitly calls SYS_newfstatat and SYS_statx (fixture lines 100-108) and asserts on the returned sizes.

findings.title: SimControl device base 0xe0080000 re-declared as a third private magic constant
findings.detail: loader.c line 24 defines `#define HTIF_MMIO_BASE 0xe0080000UL`; the same address already exists as `SIM_EXIT_ADDR 0xe0080000UL` in runtime/vplat_syscalls.c line 19 (and as a literal in runtime/crt0.S line 101). runtime/htif_client.h is the declared owner of the SimControl device layout (it documents 'SimControl exit @0xe0080000' in prose and defines WIN_DATA_VA 0xe0080840; htif_client.c defines the doorbell 0xe0080028 and slots 0xe0080800). loader.c's own comment (lines 21-23) even points at htif_client.h as the source of this layout, then re-declares the base privately anyway. Hoisting one `SIM_CONTROL_BASE` (and the 0x1000 window size) into htif_client.h and deriving SIM_EXIT_ADDR / HTIF_MMIO_BASE from it gives the C sites one source of truth (crt0.S is assembly and can stay as-is).
findings.safety: All three sites hold the identical value today; replacing two private defines with one shared define whose value is unchanged produces identical object code.
findings.verify_with: scripts/build_all.sh runtime + tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_boot.sh and tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_loader.sh (loader overlap check against the MMIO window) + any tests/vplat/ smoke test (_exit path).

findings.title: Linux errno constants defined twice across mm.c and syscall.c
findings.detail: mm.c lines 20-22 define ENOMEM 12, EINVAL 22, ENOSYS 38; syscall.c lines 103-106 define EINVAL 22, ENOTTY 25, ERANGE 34, ENOSYS 38 -- EINVAL and ENOSYS are defined in both files. They cannot use the toolchain's <errno.h> (newlib's ENOSYS is 88, not Linux's 38, which is why local defines exist at all -- vlinux must return LINUX numbers to the glibc app), so the right home is one small vlinux-local header (e.g. runtime/linux/linux_errno.h) included by both, preventing the two copies from drifting when the next syscall needs a new errno.
findings.safety: Same numeric values, moved to a shared header; preprocessor output for both TUs is unchanged.
findings.verify_with: make -C runtime/linux, then tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_file.sh (exercises -EINVAL/-ENOSYS paths via readlinkat/getdents64 probing in glibc) and test_vlinux_mmap.sh (-ENOMEM/-EINVAL paths).

findings.title: rt_linux fixture droppings (rt_linux_file_test.tmp, rt_linux_mmap_test.tmp) land untracked at repo root
findings.detail: git status shows untracked rt_linux_file_test.tmp and rt_linux_mmap_test.tmp at the repo root. Their origin is proven: tests/fixtures/rt_linux_file.c line 31 and rt_linux_mmap.c line 39 open the relative paths "rt_linux_file_test.tmp"/"rt_linux_mmap_test.tmp", and tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_file.sh runs the simulator with `cd "$ROOT"` (line 68), so the HTIF host-side relay resolves the guest's relative path against the repo root and creates the files there. .gitignore already has a section for exactly this pattern ('# Notebook/tutorial scratch at repo root', lines 12-20 with /hello.c etc.) but has no entry for these; every vlinux file-io test run re-dirties the working tree. findings.title: HDRS dependency list omits ../htif_client.h, which syscall.c and mm.c include
findings.detail: The vlinux.elf rule's HDRS (Makefile lines 46-47) lists manifest.h loader.h stack.h mm.h ../ecall_hook.h and the hybrid state_abi.h, but not ../htif_client.h -- which runtime/linux/syscall.c line 14 and mm.c line 11 both #include (it defines WIN_DATA_VA/WIN_DATA_SIZE and every VH_SYS_* number the dispatch uses). The omission happens to be masked today because the phony `rtlib` prerequisite (lines 42-43, .PHONY line 32) forces vlinux.elf to rebuild on every make invocation regardless of HDRS -- which also means the HDRS list is currently decorative. Adding ../htif_client.h keeps the declared dependency list truthful for anyone who later removes the always-rebuild behavior.
findings.safety: Adding a prerequisite can only add rebuild triggers, and the target already rebuilds unconditionally via the phony rtlib prereq, so build outputs and behavior are unchanged.
findings.verify_with: make -C runtime/linux twice (second run still succeeds/rebuilds identically); tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_boot.sh confirms the produced vlinux.elf boots.

findings.title: REQUIRED_ELFS hand-duplicates the RT_TESTS fixture list and has drifted by 6 fixtures
findings.detail: REQUIRED_ELFS (lines 63-69) exists only to decide whether to run `make -C tests/fixtures -j` (lines 70-77), but it is a second hand-maintained copy of the fixture names already encoded in RT_TESTS (lines 83-108) and SERIAL_RT_TESTS (lines 124-127). It has drifted: RT_TESTS drives rt_m_ext_counters, rt_m_ext_trigcause, rt_c_static_buf, rt_c_dlm_data, rt_c_ilm_code, and rt_c_hvm_data (all present in tests/fixtures/ and tests/fixtures/Makefile lines 32, 51-52), yet none of the six appear in REQUIRED_ELFS. On a checkout where the older ELFs exist but any of these six is missing (e.g. a stale build dir after pulling the commit that added them), need_build stays 0, the auto-build guard does not fire, and those tests FAIL with a missing ELF instead of rebuilding. Structural fix: derive the required set from the FIXTURE= fields of RT_TESTS + SERIAL_RT_TESTS instead of a second literal list.
findings.safety: When all ELFs are present (the normal case) the derived check evaluates the same way and no make runs, so behavior is identical. When some are missing it triggers the exact same `make -C tests/fixtures -j` already used for the older fixtures; the Makefile builds all fixtures anyway, so no new build steps are introduced.
findings.verify_with: rm tests/fixtures/rt_m_ext_counters.elf && FILTER=rt_m_ext_counters bash scripts/run_e2e.sh (should auto-rebuild and pass, not fail with a missing ELF); then a full `bash scripts/run_e2e.sh` stays green.

findings.title: config.env bootstrap (copy-template + source + validate) duplicated between build_runtime.sh and setup.sh, with a third variant in tests/lib/paths.sh
findings.detail: build_runtime.sh lines 20-40 re-implement what setup.sh lines 66-86 already do: if config.env is missing, copy config.env.example to config.env (identical error message wording for the missing-template case), source it, and validate HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has a bin/ dir. tests/lib/paths.sh lines 17-19 carry a third, simpler variant (source only if HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset). The copies also diverge in precedence: build_runtime.sh captures exported HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 first so the environment wins (lines 21-34) and its header (line 10) claims this is 'like setup.sh' -- but setup.sh sources config.env unconditionally at line 76, so the file's plain assignments clobber any exported HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/QEMU_BIN_DIR/VSIM_BIN_DIR. Extracting one shared loader (e.g. scripts/lib/config_env.sh) sourced by both scripts removes the duplication and makes the precedence choice live in exactly one place. Note the shared helper must stay source-safe for setup.sh's function-wrapped zsh/bash dual-mode context.
findings.safety: Pure extraction: keep each caller's current precedence semantics behind the shared function (a load_config_env with an env-wins flag, or two entry points) so both scripts execute the same statements they do today. No command lines, validation messages, or exit codes need to change.
findings.verify_with: bash tests/setup/test_setup_exports.sh (setup.sh export contract) plus bash scripts/build_runtime.sh and bash tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_runtime_dual.sh.

findings.title: Header says VSIM_BIN defaults to 'first sim_* under $VSIM_BIN_DIR' but the code pins sim_ax45mpv_premium
findings.detail: The env-override doc at line 8 states the VSIM_BIN default is 'first sim_* under $VSIM_BIN_DIR'. The code (lines 32-43) deliberately defaults to $VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium (the canonical single-hart engine, with an 11-line comment explaining why first-sim_* is wrong on multicore builds like sim_ax45mpv_mp2) and only falls back to the first sim_* when the canonical engine is not built. findings.title: Disposition 'EXCL_RO' used for mintstatus is missing from the module docstring's disposition list
findings.detail: The docstring (lines 14-27) enumerates all dispositions the classifier can emit, but the OVERRIDE map assigns mintstatus 'EXCL_RO' (line 56), a value not in that list, and the committed tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv line 53 carries it (0xFB1,MRO,mintstatus,...,EXCL_RO). The consumer tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py treats any decision outside its TRANSPORT set (line 38) as excluded, so behavior is fine, but the documented enum contradicts the code. Note mintstatus is priv=MRO, so without the override the structural default at lines 111-112 would classify it CONST_RO anyway; the minimal doc fix is to add EXCL_RO to the docstring (or fold it into CONST_RO and regenerate the CSV, which check_coverage.py handles identically -- but that touches a committed snapshot, so the docstring addition is the safe structural fix).

findings.title: Header claims 'an exported value in your shell takes precedence' -- false for the setup.sh path
findings.detail: Lines 7-9 say 'Both setup.sh and the test harness scripts load ./config.env at startup, so an exported value in your shell takes precedence; this file fills in the gaps'. That is true for tests/lib/paths.sh (sources config.env only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is unset, lines 17-19) and for scripts/build_runtime.sh (captures exported values first, lines 21-34), but false for setup.sh: it sources config.env unconditionally (setup.sh line 76), and config.env's plain assignments (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=..., QEMU_BIN_DIR=..., VSIM_BIN_DIR=...) overwrite any exported value. A user exporting QEMU_BIN_DIR to point at a different QEMU and then running `source ./setup.sh` silently gets the config.env value instead, contrary to this comment. Structural fix: correct the comment to state that setup.sh always takes the config.env values (or scope the precedence claim to the harness scripts). Making setup.sh honor the environment would be a behavioral change and is out of scope here; this pairs with the env-resolution consolidation finding in build_runtime.sh.
findings.safety: Comment-only edit in a template file that is copied verbatim to the gitignored config.env; no script reads the comments.

findings.title: profile silently ignores run-only flags --runtime and --step-timeout-ms, contradicting its own reject-loudly policy
findings.detail: cmd_profile.cpp:241-263 declares 'reject run-only flags loudly instead of silently ignoring them' and rejects --mode/--trigger/--pc-start/--pc-end/--verify/--kanata/--gdb/--gdb-port/--print-memmap. But cli.cpp:111 and :116 parse --runtime and --step-timeout-ms for every subcommand, and grep shows both are consumed only by cmd_run.cpp (lines 186-804 for cli.runtime, 613 for cli.step_timeout_ms) - cmd_profile never reads them and never rejects them. So 'andesim profile --runtime linux app.elf' silently profiles the bare-metal app WITHOUT the vlinux proxy kernel (a different workload than the hybrid run the report's measure: windows target), and --step-timeout-ms is silently dropped. tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_profile.sh section 2g ('run-only flags are rejected loudly, not silently ignored') tests only --trigger/--mode/--verify, so the gap is untested.
findings.safety: This is a behavior gap, not a structural refactor - flagged for separate handling per instructions. The fix (two more rows in the runonly[] array at cmd_profile.cpp:247-257) only turns a silent ignore into exit 2 with the existing 'not a profile option' message; no passing use case changes because the flags currently do nothing under profile.
findings.verify_with: Add 'expect 2 "not a profile option" ... profile --runtime linux ...' and '... --step-timeout-ms 5 ...' lines to section 2g of tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_profile.sh, then run that script.

findings.title: Engine-sync probe (--print-qemu-config -> stage cfg -> extract -cpu -> default fallback) is written three times
findings.detail: cmd_profile.cpp:313-325 runs run_process({acc->bin_path, "--print-qemu-config"}, 5000), then stage_qemu_cfg(wd, probe), then qemu_cpu_from_cfg(probe.out) with a kDefaultQemuCpu fallback. run_plan.cpp:396-404 does the identical sequence (probe, stage_qemu_cfg, qemu_cpu_from_cfg; the kDefaultQemuCpu fallback applied at line 304). cmd_run.cpp:509-513 (--print-memmap path) runs the same probe a third time with its own inline success check that re-states stage_qemu_cfg's condition (spawn_failed/timed_out/rc==0, cf. run_plan.cpp:145). The 5000 ms timeout is a bare literal in cmd_profile.cpp:317 and cmd_run.cpp:510 while run_plan.cpp:109 names it kQemuCfgProbeMs in an anonymous namespace - the constant already exists but is not exported. A single helper next to stage_qemu_cfg in run_plan.{hpp,cpp} (probe bin -> {cfg_path, cpu}) would serve all three call sites and retire the duplicated timeout literal.
findings.safety: Pure extraction: the helper performs the same calls in the same order with the same 5000 ms timeout and the same empty-string fallbacks; each caller keeps its own warning/log wording. No argv token or diagnostic changes.
findings.verify_with: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_profile.sh (sections 2a/2c/2e assert the derived -cpu/-readconfig and the probe-failure fallback), tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_print_memmap.sh, tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_dry_run.sh, and build/driver unit tests (plan_test).

findings.title: cmd_exists()/find_first() re-implement the $PATH walk that cmd_doctor.cpp already has as which()
findings.detail: cmd_profile.cpp:51-68 (cmd_exists: split $PATH on ':', access(dir+"/"+cmd, X_OK); find_first: first existing candidate) duplicates cmd_doctor.cpp:125-141 (which(): same $PATH split + access X_OK, returning the full path, plus a !is_directory guard and trailing-'/' handling). Two independent PATH-resolvers in the same driver binary; cmd_exists(cmd) for a '/'-containing cmd is a one-line access() special case on top. Hoisting which() into a shared header (e.g. strutil.hpp or process.hpp) and expressing cmd_exists as a wrapper removes one implementation.
findings.safety: Behavior-preserving for all existing call sites: cmd_profile only ever asks about toolchain binary names (objdump/addr2line variants), for which the extra !is_directory guard in the doctor version is a strict-superset check that cannot flip a real executable from found to not-found; the '/'-path short-circuit stays in the wrapper. cmd_doctor keeps its exact which() semantics.
findings.verify_with: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_profile.sh (resolve_objdump/addr2line paths exercised via the report path) and the doctor rows in tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f0.sh / running ./andesim doctor manually; both are read-only checks of tool discovery.

findings.title: Third hand-rolled mkdtemp scratch-dir implementation; also hardcodes /tmp unlike the other two
findings.detail: The driver has three mkdtemp implementations: tempdir.cpp:11-18 make_temp_dir() (fs::temp_directory_path + prefix-XXXXXX, the designated shared helper per tempdir.hpp:1-2), run_plan.cpp:368-379 (inline temp_directory_path + "andesim-plan-XXXXXX" + mkdtemp), and cmd_profile.cpp:216-231 (struct Workdir with the literal template "/tmp/andesim-profile.XXXXXX"). cmd_profile's copy is the only one that hardcodes /tmp, ignoring $TMPDIR, and tempdir.hpp's comment ('currently: --runtime linux's manifest staging') documents that the shared helper has only one consumer while two near-copies exist. Workdir's RAII remove_all is 3 lines on top of make_temp_dir(); run_plan already does its own remove_all at line 453.
findings.safety: Replacing both open-coded sites with make_temp_dir() keeps the same create-unique-dir semantics and each caller's existing cleanup. The only observable delta is cmd_profile's workdir moving from a hardcoded /tmp to the system temp dir (identical when $TMPDIR is unset, which is the tested configuration); no test asserts the /tmp prefix - test_andes_sim_profile.sh greps the staged cfg as '-readconfig .*/qemu\.cfg', path-agnostic. findings.title: Plugin header comment says backward edge is 'strictly less than'; the code (and docs/profile.md) use <=
findings.detail: The file comment (lines 4-6) reads 'when the next executed translation block starts at a PC strictly less than the last instruction PC of the previously executed TB'. The actual test at line 75 is 'tbi->tb_start <= st->last_tail_pc' - equality included, which is what counts a one-instruction self-loop (a single-insn TB whose start IS its last-insn PC, e.g. 'loop: j loop' or a 1-insn vector-tail loop). docs/profile.md:72-74 documents the <= form ('starts at a PC `<=` that remembered PC'), so the in-file comment is the odd one out and misdescribes a deliberate boundary condition.
findings.safety: Comment-only edit ('strictly less than' -> 'less than or equal to (equality = a single-instruction self-loop)'); no code change, cannot alter behavior.
findings.verify_with: make -C qemu_plugin still compiles; tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotIterationLoop_measure.sh and build/driver/andesim-profile-test are unaffected by a comment.

findings.title: profile_qemu_argv hardcodes the AE350 QEMU boot tokens a third time, with drifted flag spellings
findings.detail: profile_qemu_argv (profile.cpp:426-448) hand-builds '-M andes_ae350 ... -nographic -semihosting -bios {elf}'. The same boot shape is hardcoded twice more in engine_registry.cpp's builtin qemu descriptor: the fast-leg template (lines 53-60) and the standalone template (lines 71-74), both spelled '-machine andes_ae350 ... -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native -bios {elf}'. The spellings have already drifted (-M vs -machine; bare -semihosting [target=auto] vs -semihosting-config target=native), so a future machine/semihosting change must be found and made in three places. Minimal structural fix: align profile_qemu_argv's spellings with the descriptor's (-machine, -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native) and note the other sites in a comment; full unification (deriving profile's base argv from the builtin descriptor template) is a larger design change and NOT proposed here.
findings.safety: -M is a documented QEMU alias of -machine (identical parse). '-semihosting' means target=auto, which resolves to native exactly when no gdb client is attached - profile never passes -gdb/-S and cmd_profile rejects --gdb (line 254), so target=native is the value both spellings produce on every profile run. The exact-argv expectations in profile_test.cpp:198-226 must be updated with the same token strings (test-only edit, same commit).
findings.verify_with: build/driver/andesim-profile-test (test_profile_qemu_argv, after updating its expected tokens) plus tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotIterationLoop_measure.sh, which runs the real QEMU profile command end-to-end and would catch any flag QEMU rejects.

findings.title: libhybrid_handoff.so prerequisite list omits 3 of the 6 hybrid headers the .c includes (and the vendored qemu-plugin.h)
findings.detail: hybrid_handoff.c lines 5-12 include hybrid/handoff_site.h, hybrid/insn_match.h, hybrid/reg_names.h, hybrid/state_abi.h, hybrid/v_drain_policy.h, hybrid/write_mask.h, and <qemu-plugin.h>. The Makefile rule (lines 35-39) lists only state_abi.h, state_abi_check.h, insn_match.h, write_mask.h. findings.title: --print-memmap 'OVERLAPS the reserved V-scratch page' branch is unreachable
findings.detail: In run_hybrid, the L26/F3 overlap guard (cmd_run.cpp:468-483) runs unconditionally, including in memmap_only mode: it computes scratch_gpa = physical_mmap_bytes(mem) - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES, which equals mem exactly (shm.cpp:87-89 defines physical_mmap_bytes as program_bytes + HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES), and returns fail() when elf_load_top(elf_path) > scratch_gpa. The --print-memmap block at lines 504-532 executes only after that guard passed, and calls the same deterministic elf_load_top on the same elf_path, so at line 526 'top <= mem' is always true and the else-branch string 'OVERLAPS the reserved V-scratch page; raise --mem-size' (lines 528-529) can never print. Note the design tension: the comment at lines 403-406 says the ELF 'only adds the fit-vs-scratch note' in memmap mode, but the hard guard fires first - if the OVERLAPS note was meant to be reachable under --print-memmap, the guard would need a memmap_only skip (a behavioral choice, out of structural scope).
findings.safety: Removing the unreachable ternary else-branch (leaving the unconditional 'fits DRAM' note, or hoisting the guard result) cannot change any observable output, because no input reaches that branch: any ELF with top > mem already exited with the fail() diagnostic before the memmap block runs.
findings.verify_with: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_print_memmap.sh (asserts the map output and gating) plus a manual `./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap` with an oversized ELF showing the fail() path fires first, before and after the change.

findings.title: LOAD x0 in the trap-exit register restore is an architectural no-op
findings.detail: Line 101 `LOAD x0, 0*REGBYTES(sp)` loads the frame slot back into x0; RISC-V discards writes to x0, so the instruction has no architectural effect (the memory read is from the just-written stack frame, same page as the adjacent restores, so no fault-behavior difference either). The matching STORE x0 at line 24 IS load-bearing - it defines regs[0]=0 in the frame contract documented by ecall_hook.h ('regs[N] is xN for N in {0,1,3..31}') - so only the LOAD should go. This file is vendor-derived (Andes copyright header, 'NOT ... for production'), so the team may prefer keeping it verbatim; if so, skip.
findings.safety: rd=x0 makes the instruction a no-op by ISA definition; removing it changes no register, no memory, no trap behavior - only one fewer instruction on the trap-return path (not inside any measured ROI contract).

findings.title: _getcwd declares its output buffer const and casts the const away internally
